title: P1.4 buffer kernel: 4 designs in parallel, Pareto over use cases
description: mode:par over DESIGNS (not three copies of one). Every variant implements src/piece/piece.h exactly (after P1.3b amendments) and must pass tests/piece_test.c + fuzz/piece_fuzz.c unchanged. Variants, each a Sonnet worker in variants/P1.4/<name>/ who must not look at the others: (a) bptree: piece B+ tree, SoA 384 B pooled nodes, per-node byte+newline counts, path-copy snapshots (perf section 3 design). (b) rope: balanced rope whose leaves are pieces (store, off, len) with cached counts, rebalanced on insert, snapshot = root share (xi-editor style). (c) flat: piece table as one contiguous array of pieces with a cursor cache + a sparse prefix-sum skip index rebuilt lazily; snapshot = copy the array (cheap until ~10^5 pieces). (d) hybrid: per-line gap buffers for lines shorter than 4 KiB in an array of line records, falling back to pieces for long lines and for mmapped originals; snapshot by COW of line records. Bench matrix (bench/piece_bench.c, one file shared by all variants, written FIRST by the coordinator or the first worker and frozen): rows = use cases {1 MB code file, 1 GB log (mmap), 10 GB single line (mmap, --huge corpus), dense_short 64 MB, 10^5 random edits, 10^4 cursor-typing inserts, 10^5 undo-style reinserts, 100 snapshots alive while editing (100 tabs), line_to_byte at line 10^7}; columns = {insert p50/p99, delete p50/p99, read 300-row viewport, snapshot take, byte<->line, peak memory vs G10f, first-op latency after open, .text size}. Gates from perf: G1 edit < 0.5 ms slice, G9 10^5 random edits in a 1 GB mmap < 1 s, snapshot < 1 us, G10f. Decision: Pareto front over the matrix; if one design dominates, promote it; if the front has 2+ points, an Opus best-of synthesis bead takes the dominant design and borrows the others' winning tricks. Then a Codex deep review. Record everything in docs/decisions/P1.4.md. Rules: see CLAUDE.md.
